reason: The checker question is 'is the static type of this call / await / tagged-template expression exactly `void`?'. Position logic (statement, ternary branch, &&/|| chains, arrow shorthand option) ports exactly. The port can only name callees that are void by convention (console.*). Anything else needs the callee's declared return type, and for `await` the awaited type of a Promise<void>. Checker APIs: getTypeAtLocation(call) flag Void (:90). Line 11 needs the awaited type of Promise<void>; console.* voids come from lib.

evidence.why: `const x = doIt();` is void only because `declare function doIt(): void;` (line 18) says so. The same syntax with any value-returning function is valid.
`await doAsync()` is void only because doAsync returns Promise<void>; needs awaited-type resolution
`print``` is void only via `declare function print(...): void`
